title: Mongolia: Human plague confirmed in Khovd province
summary: Mongolia’s National Centre for Zoonotic Diseases confirmed a human plague case in Khovd province after the patient consumed marmot meat. Authorities warned against hunting or handling marmots and noted that plague risk rises in summer when rural travel and marmot consumption increase. Seventeen of 21 provinces are classified as plague-risk, and early antibiotic treatment is critical.
content:
Mongolia’s National Centre for Zoonotic Diseases (NCZD) reported Friday the confirmation of a human plague case in Khovd province in the western part of the country.

The patient contracted the disease after consuming marmot meat while visiting Ulaankhus soum in the neighboring Bayan-Ulgii province.

The NCZD issued a public warning urging people to avoid hunting or capturing marmots, handling their meat or internal organs, and coming into contact with dead or sick rodents.

PLAGUE primer and updated treatment recommendations

Health officials noted that the risk of plague transmission generally increases during the summer months, when more people travel to rural areas and some consume marmot meat. Mongolia has reported several cases of bubonic plague in recent years during this period, including fatal infections.

Anthrax case reported in Uvs province in western Mongolia

The NCZD said that 17 of Mongolia’s 21 provinces are currently classified as plague-risk areas, highlighting the continued need for public awareness and preventive measures.

Plague is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium, Yersinia pestis. It is found in animals throughout the world, most commonly rats but other rodents like ground squirrels, prairie dogs, chipmunks, rabbits and marmots. Fleas typically serve as the vector for plague.

Plague Doctor Mask

People can also get infected through direct contact with an infected animal, through inhalation and in the case of pneumonic plague, person to person.

Yersinia pestis is treatable with antibiotics if started early enough.

There are three forms of human plague; bubonic, septicemic and pneumonic.

## Incident Details

Mongolia’s National Centre for Zoonotic Diseases (NCZD) reported Friday the confirmation of a human plague case in Khovd province in the western part of the country.

The patient contracted the disease after consuming marmot meat while visiting Ulaankhus soum in the neighboring Bayan-Ulgii province.

## Response

The NCZD issued a public warning urging people to avoid:

- hunting or capturing marmots
- handling marmot meat or internal organs
- coming into contact with dead or sick rodents

## PLAGUE primer and updated treatment recommendations

Health officials noted that the risk of plague transmission generally increases during the summer months, when more people travel to rural areas and some consume marmot meat. Mongolia has reported several cases of bubonic plague in recent years during this period, including fatal infections.

## Other reports

Anthrax case reported in Uvs province in western Mongolia

## Geographic Risk

The NCZD said that 17 of Mongolia’s 21 provinces are currently classified as plague-risk areas, highlighting the continued need for public awareness and preventive measures.

## About plague

Plague is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. It is found in animals throughout the world, most commonly rats but also other rodents such as:

- ground squirrels
- prairie dogs
- chipmunks
- rabbits
- marmots

Fleas typically serve as the vector for plague.

People can also get infected through direct contact with an infected animal, through inhalation and, in the case of pneumonic plague, from person to person.

Yersinia pestis is treatable with antibiotics if started early enough.

There are three forms of human plague:

- bubonic
- septicemic
- pneumonic
